facts.statement: Changzuiornis was an extinct ornithuromorph bird that lived in present-day China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Changzuiornis is an extinct genus of ornithuromorph bird from the Early Cretaceous of present-day China.

facts.statement: The species Changzuiornis ahgmi was named and described in 2016 by Huang Jiandong, Wang Xia, Hu Yuanchao, Liu Jia, Jennifer A. Peteya, and Julia A. Clarke.
facts.quote: In 2016 the type species Changzuiornis ahgmi was named and described by Huang Jiandong, Wang Xia, Hu Yuanchao, Liu Jia, Jennifer A. Peteya and Julia A. Clarke.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil was found in the Aptian-aged Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, AGB5840, was found in a layer of the Jiufotang Formation dating from the Aptian.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton preserves feather remains and gastroliths.
facts.quote: It consists of an almost complete and associated skeleton with skull, compressed on a plate. It preserves feather remains and gastroliths.

facts.statement: Changzuiornis possessed an unusually long beak that reached 68% of the total skull length.
facts.quote: Changzuiornis has an unusually long rostrum, (beak) which reaches 68% of the total skull length.

facts.statement: Changzuiornis had many small teeth, most of which were located on the bottom jaw.
facts.quote: They had many teeth, most of which were located on the bottom jaw, yet they were very small, considering this bird was on the way to modern evolution.

facts.statement: Changzuiornis is classified within the Ornithurae.
facts.quote: Changzuiornis was placed in the Ornithurae.

facts.statement: Changzuiornis belongs to the family Gansuidae.
Changzuiornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that Changzuiornis might be the same genus as Juehuaornis, which would mean Juehuaornis has priority.
facts.quote: The describers suggested that Changzuiornis might be cogeneric to the closely related Juehuaornis found in the same formation, in which case the latter genus would have priority.

rejected.statement: The genus name Changzuiornis combines the Chinese word for 'longest' with the Greek word for 'bird' to reference its long beak.
rejected.quote: The generic name combines the Chinese chángzuì, 'the longest', a reference to the long beak, with a Greek ὄρνις, ornis, 'bird'.
